newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says renewable energy good for jobs, imports.
newsitem.headline: EU says renewable energy good for jobs, imports.

text.p: Increased use of renewable energy such as wood, wind, wave and solar power would help improve the environment, create new jobs and reduce dependency on imported fuels, the European Commission said on Thursday.
A Commission strategy paper called for the use of renewable energy sources to be doubled to 12 percent of total energy consumption by 2010.
"We think this is a realistic objective," Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis told a press conference stressing that renewable energy sources were not more expensive, as opponents say.
"On the contrary, a lot of these sources of renewable energy are competitive in relation to conventional sources," he said.
There are also good chances to export technology for the sector. "We are among the first worldwide," Papoutsis said, adding, however, that there were problems as well.

Obstacles to a wider use of renewables are related to market imperfections and the fact that prices of conventional fuels -- coal, oil and gas -- do not reflect the full environmental cost they impose on society, the Commission said.
The Commission would present next year a detailed strategy and an action plan to promote the use of renewables.

"Currently these renewable energy sources are far from being used to their full potential and make a disappointingly small contribution of less than six percent to the European Union's energy balance," it said in a statement.

If the EU could double this figure, "this would result in very significant reductions of CO2 (carbon dioxide) emissions by almost 400 million tonnes per year, as well as other benefits," the statement said.
The EU aims to cut CO2 emissions to 1990 levels by 2000.
Papoutsis said renewables would help reduce the dependency on imported energy, which is increasing from year to year.
It would be up to each member state to assess what renewable energy source would be best, but Papoutsis said there was a big advantage in hydroelectric as well as solar energy.
"I would say solar energy is beginning to gain ground in many regions of the European Community," he said.
The strategy paper did not make specific proposals but Papoutsis said "there could be tax changes for renewable sources of energy."
A plan to tax carbon dioxide emissions is currently blocked at the level of EU finance ministers.
